chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who sends his dog after game and it seizes it, but he does not have a knife to slaughter it with. Should he leave it until the dog kills it and then eat from it? He said: 'There is no problem.'
God, Mighty and Majestic, said: so eat from what they catch for you [5:4]
and it is not befitting that one eat from what the leopard kills.

key_terms.الْفَهْدُ: The leopard/cheetah — a wild predator whose kills are not permissible to eat
key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: The dog — specifically a trained hunting dog (kalb mu'allam)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem — standard juristic formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.يُذَكِّيهِ: Ritual slaughter (tadhkiyah) — the act of lawfully slaughtering an animal by cutting the throat while invoking God's name

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat prey killed by a hunting dog when no knife is available for slaughter?
ai.summary: Jamil ibn Darraj asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about a hunting scenario: when a man releases a trained hunting dog but has no knife to perform ritual slaughter (tadhkiyah) on the prey, is it permissible to let the dog kill the prey and eat from it? The Imam replied that there is no objection, citing Quran 5:4 as divine sanction. However, he distinguished this from prey killed by a leopard (fahd), which is not permissible to eat. This hadith illustrates the Islamic fiqh principle that trained hunting dogs act as instruments of halal hunting, obviating the need for separate ritual slaughter.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from is father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who sent his dog upon the prey, so it seized it, and there did not happen to be a knife with him to slaughter it with. Can he leave it until it (the dog) kills it and (then) he eats from it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Says [5:4] so eat from what which they catch for you,
and it is not befitting if you eat from what the leopard kills’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who sends his dog to catch a prey which the dog catches; but he does not have a knife to slaughter it and about if he can leave it alone for the dog to kill and eat thereof. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful
because Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said, ‘Eat what they catch for you’
, but it is not proper to eat what a cheetah has killed.’”
